layout.$description: Window size classes, as in Material 3, with thresholds tuned for a data-dense dashboard. A group keyed by size class is responsive: the build also writes one property that takes the value of the current class.

breakpoint.$description: Minimum window width of each size class. Compact starts at 0.

medium.$description: Tablets: two columns, navigation as a rail.

large.$description: Wide monitors: four columns, so a card never grows past 575 px.

extra-large.$description: Ultra-wide monitors: five columns, for the same reason.

columns.$description: Card columns of the overview grid.

margin.$description: Space between the content and the window edge, or the navigation.

gap.$description: Between cards, in every size class.

sidebar.$description: Full navigation beside the content on desktops. On tablets it opens over the content.

rail.$description: Navigation as icons only: the rail on tablets and the collapsed sidebar on desktops.

drawer.$description: The sidebar as a drawer on phones. It never covers more than 84% of the window.

bar.$description: Heights of the application bars, before safe areas are added.

top.$description: Top app bar: brand, search, notifications, assistant and account.

bottom.$description: Bottom app bar on phones: Alerts, Assistant, Edit, Account and Menu.

footer.$description: Footer and edit bar on tablets and desktops.

card.$description: Card heights in the overview grid. M + L = S + XL, so two columns built from different sizes end level.

touch-target.$description: Minimum hit area on touch screens.
